em.why: no pinned source states CR0.EM of the declared machine (ks386.inc CR0_EM is a bit constant only; Wine runs on the host CPU); user mode observes CR0 only through smsw, which is itself undecided; blocker: a reach certificate that no site depends on it, or an owner decision to derive it from the CPUID record

mp.why: no pinned source states CR0.MP (ks386.inc CR0_MP is a bit constant only); user mode sees it only through smsw (undecided)

ts.why: no pinned source; user mode sees TS only through smsw (undecided); Windows handles #NM transparently (lazy FPU switch), and the lazy-switch behaviour is not a pinned source

pce.why: rdpmc at CPL 3 needs CR4.PCE = 1; the SDM only defines the bit, the declared CPU's cpuid does not state it, the WDK 7.1 constants name no PCE bit and Wine 9.0 has no rdpmc case

tsd.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: is_privileged_instr intercepts only the 0F opcodes ['0x20', '0x21', '0x22', '0x23'], so rdtsc (0F 31) runs in user mode; consistent with the owner's decision that rdtsc reads the platform timer

osfxsr.why: no pinned source states CR4.OSFXSR (ks386.inc CR4_FXSR = 0x200 is a bit constant only); the declared CPU's cpuid (verify/cpuid_model.json leaf 1 EDX) advertises FXSR/SSE/SSE2, but whether the OS enabled them is not a pinned fact; blocker: an owner/L3b decision to take OS support from the CPUID record, or a reach certificate

osxmmexcpt.why: no pinned source states CR4.OSXMMEXCPT (ks386.inc CR4_XMMEXCPT = 0x400 is a bit constant only); with the initial MXCSR 0x1F80 every SIMD exception is masked, so #XM is not raised until a site unmasks it; blocker: a certificate that every ldmxcsr / fxrstor site keeps the exceptions masked (CLAUDE.md fact, not yet certified)

other_vectors.applies_to: every vector that is not a present DPL-3 gate of the 7601 IDT (249 vectors: 0x00-0x02, 0x05-0x29, 0x2f-0xff): SDM Vol 2A INT n protected-mode, a descriptor that is not an interrupt, trap or task gate, or whose DPL < CPL, is #GP(vector*8+2); entries 0x20-0x29 are zero (type 0), every other such entry is a present DPL-0 gate; the present DPL-3 gates are decided by `vectors` or listed in `excluded`
other_vectors.source: Intel SDM Vol 2 INT n and Vol 3 6.12.1.1 (a user-mode int n at a vector whose gate is not DPL 3 is #GP with error code n*8+2, IDT bit set, EXT 0, saved EIP = the int instruction); Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: segv_handler TRAP_x86_PROTFLT lines 1925-1941 (err != 0 skips is_privileged_instr; (err & 7) == 2 calls handle_interrupt, which returns FALSE at its `default` line 1804 for every vector but 0x29 and 0x2d; then EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, NumberParameters 2, ExceptionInformation[0] = 0, [1] = 0xffffffff, check_invalid_gs (line 1279) returns FALSE for opcode 0xCD); setup_exception_record line 1449: ExceptionAddress = EIP_sig, context Eip not advanced; segv_handler line 1905: rec = { 0 } so ExceptionFlags 0 (continuable). Precedence (2): MSDN and the WDK state nothing for these vectors; vector 0x29: Wine's case (__fastfail, Windows 8+) is out by the doc gate, and the 7601 IDT entry 0x29 is not present, gate type 0 (row idt, vector_0x29), so the SDM gives #GP(0x29*8+2), the same path as every vector of this row
